gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the 2 kWh kits rate cycle life to different end points (Jackery Explorer 2000 v2: 4,000+ cycles to 70%; EcoFlow DELTA 2 Max: 3,000+ cycles to 80%), or that the higher second AC figure means different things: Jackery's 4,400 W and DELTA 3 Max's 4,800 W are surge ratings, BLUETTI's 3,900 W is a mode for purely resistive loads, and EcoFlow names its 3,400 W 'X-Boost' rather than surge.
standout_why: I compared against theoutagebrief.com/2026/10/17, powersized.com/solar-generator-kits and generatorandbackup.com, all cited. Theoutagebrief.com lists continuous and surge AC, but has no cycle life and no solar voltage. Powersized.com has solar W, V and A per station, but no cycle life and no surge, and it gives one unlabeled output figure. Generatorandbackup.com mixes the two bases without saying so: it gives the DELTA 2 Max 3,000 cycles to 80% and the Explorer 1000 v2 70%, and gives no rating for the 2000 v2. It also writes 3,400 W X-Boost with the note 'not labeled as surge'. None puts the four cycle and AC-peak claims on one basis. unpluggedwatts.com (cited) would not load because of a self-signed certificate error, so it was not compared.
decides: This confirms rather than overturns ChatGPT's picks. A footnoted table shows Jackery's larger cycle count (4,000) is measured to a lower end point (70%) than EcoFlow's 3,000 (80%), so the two counts can't be compared as raw numbers. It also shows the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 (ChatGPT's 'my pick') has no published surge figure: its 3,900 W applies only to resistive loads such as heaters and kettles, not motor start-up. For a fridge or well pump, the published surge leaders are DELTA 3 Max (4,800 W) and Jackery 2000 v2 (4,400 W). The 2000 v2's 400 W solar ceiling also means any kit with more than 400 W of panels, such as the 500 W SolarSaga 500 X bundle, can't charge faster than 400 W.

findings.label: Cycle life (maker basis)
findings.note: Maker's US store text: 'Get 10 years of daily use until hitting 80% of its original capacity... 3000+ cycles.' Read with storecheck.py search.

findings.label: Cycle life (maker basis, retailer spec table)
findings.source_title: Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 2042Wh Portable Power Station (Mr. Solar)
findings.note: Jackery's own store returned HTTP 429, and its store text gives no cycle figure, so this is a retailer's spec table. The end point differs from EcoFlow's (70% vs 80%). Throughput to each end point: 4,000 × 2,042 Wh ≈ 8.2 MWh to 70%; DELTA 2 Max 3,000 × 2,048 Wh ≈ 6.1 MWh to 80%. These cannot be converted to one basis without a fade curve. If fade were linear, which is Dealectric's assumption and not a maker figure, 4,000 cycles to 70% would be about 2,670 cycles to 80% (4,000 × 20/30).

findings.label: Solar input limits
findings.value: 2 × DC 8 mm; 11–16 V ⎓ 8 A / 16–60 V ⎓ 12 A; 400 W max combined
findings.source_title: Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 2042Wh Portable Power Station (Mr. Solar)
findings.note: 400 W is the total for both ports. A kit with more than 400 W of panels (for example the 500 W SolarSaga 500 X bundle listed by powersized.com) still charges at no more than 400 W.

findings.label: AC continuous vs surge
findings.note: Maker's store text: '2200W continuous output (4400W surge)'. Read with storecheck.py search.

findings.label: Price on jackery.com
findings.note: The store text doesn't say which panels the $1,239 variant includes. Powersized.com lists Explorer 2000 v2 + 2 × SolarSaga 100 Air (200 W) at $1,239 and + 2 × SolarSaga 200W at $1,649. Our current page shows $1,649 'search listing, undated' and should be updated.

findings.label: AC continuous vs second figure
findings.value: 2,600 W continuous; 3,900 W Power Lifting for pure resistive loads only; no surge figure published
findings.note: Maker page: Power Lifting supports 'pure resistive loads of up to 3,900W'. The UK maker page (bluettipower.co.uk/products/elite-200-v2-portable-power-station) says the same. This is not a surge rating for motor start-up the way Jackery's and EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max's are.

findings.label: Solar input limits
findings.note: Arithmetic: 1,000 W ÷ 20 A = 50 V, so the full 1,000 W needs a string running at 50 V or more and still inside the 60 V limit. The 2 × 200 W kit tops out at its 400 W panel rating whatever the headline. Powersized.com gives the SP200L Voc as 24.6 V, so two in series ≈ 49 V Voc, which fits the 60 V window.

findings.label: AC continuous vs X-Boost
findings.value: 2,400 W rated; 'up to 3,400W' with X-Boost (EcoFlow doesn't call it surge)
findings.note: Store text: 'With X-Boost mode get up to 3400W output power'. Kit price $1,579 (2 × 220 W bifacial), available. Up to 1,000 W solar input. 5-year warranty on the station, 12 months on the 220 W panel.

findings.label: AC continuous vs surge vs X-Boost
findings.value: 2,400 W continuous; 4,800 W surge; X-Boost to 3,400 W
findings.note: Store text: '2400W Powerful Output: 4800W surge output. With X-Boost mode... up to 3400W'. Here EcoFlow lists surge and X-Boost as separate numbers, which confirms X-Boost is not surge. Kit price $1,249 (compare-at $1,998). The store text doesn't say which panels it includes. 'Up to 5-year warranty' = 3 years standard + 2 with app registration.
